claim: For the homogeneous optimal-control problem in Theorem 6.5 of Weng–Chitour–Mason, let \(V_\infty\) be its value function, \(K=\{x:V_\infty(x)=1\}\), and \(m=\min_{x\in K}F(x)>0\). The Lyapunov comparison rigorously gives \[T_{x_0}\leq\frac{d+\mu}{m\mu}V_\infty(x_0)^{\mu/(d+\mu)}.\] The coefficient required by this proof is the minimum of the running cost on the unit value-function level set, not its maximum; an admissible anisotropic example has distinct minimum and maximum. This corrects the displayed comparison argument and does not claim that the printed maximum-based numerical bound is false by every possible argument.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity: The minimum-based settling-time bound is proved from the stated HJB and homogeneity assumptions. The maximum-based coefficient in the cited proof is not justified by its displayed differential inequality; no trajectory-level counterexample to the printed numerical estimate is claimed. No independent audit or independent validation has been performed.
title: Correct level-set constant for a homogeneous finite-time control bound
